title: Rate and Speed: Speed, Distance, Time and Unit Conversion

key_big: Speed = distance ÷ time. Distance = speed × time. Time = distance ÷ speed.
key_sub: Change minutes to hours by dividing by 60. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
body_html:
How it works

Speed = distance ÷ time, distance = speed × time, time = distance ÷ speed. Make sure the units match: for km/h use km and hours.

Minutes must be changed to hours by dividing by 60: 45 minutes = 0.75 hours, and 1.5 hours = 1 hour 30 minutes.

Density = mass ÷ volume, usually in g/cm³. Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.

Example

A car travels 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Find its speed.

2 hours 30 minutes = 2.5 hours.

150 ÷ 2.5 = 60.

Answer: 60 km/h

Example

Write 2.4 hours in hours and minutes.

0.4 × 60 = 24 minutes.

Answer: 2 hours 24 minutes

Example

Convert 72 km/h into m/s.

72 000 m in 3600 s.

72 000 ÷ 3600 = 20.

Answer: 20 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Reading 1.5 hours as 1 hour 50 minutes. It is 1 hour 30 minutes.
  • Using minutes as hours: 40 minutes is 2/3 of an hour, not 0.4.
  • Dividing the wrong way: time = distance ÷ speed, not speed ÷ distance.
  • Finding average speed by averaging the speeds instead of total distance ÷ total time.

faq.q: What is the formula for speed?
faq.a: Speed = distance ÷ time. Rearranged, distance = speed × time and time = distance ÷ speed.

faq.q: How do I change minutes into hours?
How do I convert km/h to m/s?
faq.a: Multiply by 1000 to get metres per hour, then divide by 3600. In short, divide by 3.6.
Density = mass ÷ volume. It tells you how heavy a material is for its size, for example 19.3 g/cm³ for gold.

items.q: On a distance–time graph, what does a horizontal line show?
c: The object is moving at a steady speed
items.e: The distance does not change, so the object is not moving (stationary).

items.q: On a distance–time graph, what does a steeper straight line show?
items.e: The gradient of a distance–time graph is the speed. Steeper means faster.
